story-summary.description: Add real-time status updates for all MCP tool calls to show users which tools Annie is calling and their results. This provides transparency into how Annie gathers information (portfolio data, stock analysis, memory retrieval, etc.).
story-summary.user-story: As a user, I want to see which tools Annie is calling and their results, so that I understand how Annie is gathering information.

acceptance-criteria.criterion: Tool Call Start Status: Emit "🔧 Calling {tool_name}..." before tool execution. Tool name must be human-readable (e.g., "get_portfolio" not internal ID).

Tool Result Status: Emit "✅ {tool_name} complete: {brief_result}" after completion. Brief result examples: - get_portfolio: "3 holdings, $15,420 value" - get_stock_data: "AAPL $175.50 (+2.3%)" - internet_search: "Found 5 results" - get_user_profile: "Profile loaded (67% complete)" Result summary must be concise (<50 chars) and informative.
Tool Error Status: Emit "⚠️ {tool_name} failed: {brief_error}" on failure. Error message must be user-friendly (not stack trace). Processing continues (existing graceful degradation).

All MCP Tools Instrumented: All tools must emit status updates: - get_portfolio (with optional include_prices) - add_holding, update_holding, remove_holding, clear_portfolio - get_stock_data, get_stock_history - get_user_profile - store_memory, retrieve_memories - internet_search (if MCP-based, not Grok Live Search)

dependency.description: Requires emit_status() function and StatusContext infrastructure to be complete. This story instruments the MCP client to call emit_status() before/after tool execution.

implementation-approach.recommended-approach:
Option B: Wrapper in MCP client (single instrumentation point, easier to maintain).
Modify backend/api/mcp_client.py:call_tool() method to: 1. Emit status before tool execution: emit_status(f"Calling {tool_name}...", icon="🔧") 2. Execute tool (existing code) 3. Emit status after success: emit_status(f"{tool_name} complete: {summary}", icon="✅") 4. Emit status on error: emit_status(f"{tool_name} failed: {brief_error}", icon="⚠️")
This approach instruments all tools with a single change, vs decorating each tool individually.
implementation-approach.alternative-approach: Option A: Decorator on each tool handler (more verbose, harder to maintain). Would require adding @with_status() decorator to every tool handler in mcp_server/tools.py. Not recommended due to maintenance burden.

file.description: MCP client that executes tools via JSON-RPC 2.0. Contains call_tool() method that is the single point of instrumentation for all tool calls.

key-code-section.description: call_tool() method with @observe decorator for Langfuse tracing. This is where status emission should be added: - Before line 298 (before HTTP request): emit_status(f"Calling {tool_name}...", "🔧") - After line 367 (after success): emit_status(f"{tool_name} complete: {summary}", "✅") - In exception handlers: emit_status(f"{tool_name} failed: {error}", "⚠️")
key-code-section.code-snippet:

# INSTRUMENTATION POINT 1: Emit "Calling {tool_name}..." status here

# ... parse response ...
logger.info("Tool execution completed", extra={...})
# INSTRUMENTATION POINT 2: Emit "Complete: {summary}" status here

file.purpose: Unit tests for status summarizers. Test each tool summarizer with realistic result shapes. Test error handling and fallback behavior.

technical-notes.note: emit_status() is fire-and-forget with <10ms overhead (Story 11.1). Safe to call multiple times per tool execution without performance impact.

Tool summarizers must handle both success and error result shapes gracefully. All tools return {"status": "error", "message": "..."} on failure. Summarizers should extract user-friendly error from "message" field.

get_portfolio has two result shapes depending on include_prices parameter: - include_prices=false: Fast query, no total_value/gain_loss fields - include_prices=true: Enriched with prices, includes total_value and totals Summarizer must handle both cases.
Internet search tool (MCP-based) may not exist yet - Epic 4 may use Grok Live Search instead. Summarizer should include placeholder for future MCP internet_search tool.

Error messages from MCP tools vary: - Network errors: "Portfolio service unavailable. Please try again later." - Validation errors: "Invalid ticker format: 'xyz'. Ticker must be..." - 404 errors: "Holding not found: You don't have AAPL in your portfolio." Summarizer should truncate to 50 chars and preserve meaning.
Status emitter uses contextvar pattern (similar to Langfuse tracing). No-op if StatusContext not active - safe to call from anywhere. Must import emit_status before use in mcp_client.py.

example-implementation.code:
# backend/api/mcp_client.py (modifications)
from api.status import emit_status from api.status_summarizers import summarize_tool_result
# In call_tool() method:
async def call_tool(self, tool_name: str, arguments: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None): # ... existing setup code ...
try: # ... JSON-RPC request setup ...
logger.info("Calling MCP tool", extra={"tool_name": tool_name, ...})
# INSTRUMENTATION: Emit start status emit_status(f"Calling {tool_name}...", icon="🔧")
response = await self.client.post(url, json=json_rpc_request, ...)
# ... parse response and extract tool_result ...
logger.info("Tool execution completed", extra={...})
# INSTRUMENTATION: Emit success status with summary summary = summarize_tool_result(tool_name, tool_result) emit_status(f"{tool_name} complete: {summary}", icon="✅")
return tool_result
except httpx.TimeoutException as e: logger.error("Tool execution timeout", extra={...})
# INSTRUMENTATION: Emit error status emit_status(f"{tool_name} failed: Request timed out", icon="⚠️")
raise MCPNetworkError(f"Tool '{tool_name}' timed out", e)
# ... (similar for other exception handlers)

performance-considerations.consideration: emit_status() has <10ms overhead (Story 11.1 requirement). Safe to call 2-3 times per tool execution without degrading p95 latency.
Summarizers must be fast (<1ms) - simple string formatting only. No expensive operations (no LLM calls, no network requests).
Tool result truncation to 50 chars prevents excessive status message length. Telegram message edit API has rate limits - keep status concise.

edge-cases.case: Tool returns malformed result (missing expected fields): Summarizer catches exception and falls back to generic "Complete".

Tool execution fails before HTTP request (validation error): Status emitter may not be called if error happens before emit_status() line. This is acceptable - validation errors are rare and fast-fail.
Multiple tools called in parallel (future enhancement): Each tool call is independent, emits its own status. Status emitter handles concurrent calls via contextvars isolation.

StatusContext not initialized (emit_status() called outside request): emit_status() is no-op when no context active (Story 11.1 requirement). Safe to call from anywhere, including tools invoked outside streaming.
